name: Compile-time payload extraction from a test fixture (XZ-style, effect-bearing)
description: Models how the XZ Utils backdoor was delivered: the payload hides inside a test-data file that no one reviews as code, and an injected build step reads it during compilation. Appends a custom_target to the top-level meson.build that runs at compile time, reads the first bytes of a test fixture under t/, and writes them to a PWNED_fixture marker (standing in for splicing the payload into a build output). The build and tests still pass. Unlike op_005/op_013, the attack's key action (the compile phase reading a test file) happens inside the source tree, so a phase-isolation checker such as Foreman can observe it.

placeholders.MESON_BUILD: relative path to the meson.build being modified

template.replacement_value: custom_target('fixture_hook', output: 'fixture_hook.stamp', command: ['sh', '-c', 'head -c 64 "$0" > /tmp/PWNED_fixture_{{MARKER_ID}} && touch "$1"', meson.project_source_root() / '{{FIXTURE}}', '@OUTPUT@'], build_by_default: true)

preconditions: project uses Meson; a custom_target with build_by_default runs during meson compile, not setup
the fixture file exists in the source tree and the clean compile phase does not read it
the build is from a release-style tree (no .git), otherwise git's version script reads every tracked file during compile and hides the read
